trigger: Confirmed security incident affecting customer data
deadline: Without undue delay and within 72 hours of confirmation
notify: Each affected customer's security contact (then the customer administrator)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, all 45 customers. Send a short initial notice when facts are thin, then update at least every 72 hours

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the covered entity
trigger: Breach of security of a system the company maintains for a customer, involving personal information of Florida residents as defined in 501.171(1)(g) (here: names with Social Security numbers on W-9s)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe the breach occurred. Give the customer all information it needs to give its own notices
notify: Each affected customer (the covered entity), which then gives notice under 501.171(3) and (4)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 4,100 Florida individuals with Social Security numbers on W-9s. The company may send notices on a customer's behalf under 501.171(6)(b), but a failure is then treated as the customer's violation, so only on the customer's written request

obligation: Service-provider and data-maintainer notices in other states
citation: State breach notification statutes (each state where affected individuals reside)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information the company maintains but does not own
deadline: Varies by state (often 'immediately' or 'without unreasonable delay' after discovery)
notify: Owner or licensee of the data (each affected customer)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - vendors with Social Security numbers live in about 20 states besides Florida. Counsel checks each state's maintainer duty; in practice the 72-hour DPA notice and the Florida 10-day notice are sent to every affected customer at the same time

obligation: State data breach notification to individuals
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state; in Florida a name with a Social Security number is personal information under 501.171(1)(g)1.a.(I); counsel checks each other state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Customers' duty for customer vendor data (they own it). The company supplies affected-record lists by state and, on written request, mailing support. The company's own duty applies only to data it owns (next rows)

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals (company-owned data)
trigger: Breach of personal information the company owns: customer user sign-in credentials (501.171(1)(g)1.b., a user name or email with a password that would permit access) or its own employees' data
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred. Not required if, after investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines in writing that identity theft or other financial harm is not likely; keep that determination 5 years and send it to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days (501.171(4)(c))
applies_at_this_tier: Only for company-owned data. Counsel decides whether salted, hashed passwords are 'secured' and therefore excluded (501.171(1)(g)2.); the company plans to reset all customer passwords either way

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida, where the company is the covered entity
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension applies only to the notice to individuals, not to this notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Only as covered entity (company-owned data). About 900 customer users in total, so the 500-Floridian count is unlikely to be met for company-owned data. For customer vendor data this is each customer's duty

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Only as covered entity. Unlikely for company-owned data; likely for any customer whose Florida vendor count with Social Security numbers exceeds 1,000

obligation: Law enforcement report (voluntary) and the Florida consultation
citation: Fla. Stat. 501.171(4)(c); FBI IC3 and CISA reporting (voluntary)
trigger: Confirmed theft of customer data or an extortion demand
deadline: As soon as practicable (day 0 to 2); before any extortion decision
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary, but it is also the law enforcement consultation Florida requires before any written 'no harm' determination, and full and timely reporting is an OFAC mitigating factor

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a payment to stop publication or return of stolen data
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties. POL-03 4.7 also requires Chief Executive Officer, counsel, and insurer approval. Paying does not remove any notice duty

deadline: Per policy (call the carrier's breach hotline before hiring outside vendors)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal. Panel counsel and forensics are engaged through the hotline

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident / ransom payment reports (pending final rule)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: 72 hours (covered incident); 24 hours (ransom payment) - not yet effective
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (not in effect). Proposed scope keys on entities above the SBA size standard or meeting sector criteria; the company is far below the size standard. Recheck when the rule is final

trigger: Breach of CPNI held by a telecommunications carrier or interconnected VoIP provider
deadline: As soon as practicable, no later than 7 business days after reasonable determination; customers only after 7 full business days post-LE notice (unless urgent/LE directs otherwise)
notify: USSS and FBI via FCC central reporting facility; then customers
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is not a carrier or VoIP provider and holds no CPNI

obligation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident disclosure
trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within four business days after determining the incident is material

obligation: Bank service provider notification (IT/data processors serving banks)
trigger: Incident that materially disrupts or degrades covered services to a banking organization customer for 4 or more hours
deadline: As soon as possible when an incident materially disrupts/degrades covered services for 4+ hours
notify: Bank-designated point of contact at each affected banking organization customer
applies_at_this_tier: No - no banking organization customers. Recheck if a bank signs up

citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or Kaspersky covered article in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - Cris Santos Company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
